title: meridian-bank-integration-call-notes-2026-04-01
body:
Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood PM), Luis Gomez (Redwood SRE), Tom Ellis (Meridian - Head of Platform), Sara Hwang (Meridian - Security), Nathan Cole (Meridian - Payments)

Quick summary:
- Intro + goals: Meridian wants to evaluate Redwood Private for payment fraud detection model serving + embedding store for transaction vectors. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS integration, latency SLOs (tail latency), and failover to hosted while private deploy boots.
- Current infra: Meridian runs in GCP us-east4, uses internal KMS + HSM for key material, has strict audit requirements and quarterly pen test. They have existing microservice for inference but high variation in tail latency at scale.

Key requirements (explicit):
- Data residency: all logs and payloads must stay in customer VPC. No PII can be stored outside KMS-protected S3 buckets in their account.
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with their Cloud HSM for model keys and encryption at rest. Need clear doc of supported KMS providers and steps.
- Latency/SLOs: 95th percentile < 120ms for <=512 token requests for the fraud model at 100 QPS sustained. 99th percentile target < 350ms.
- Throughput: starting baseline 100 QPS with capability to burst to 500 QPS during batch-clearing windows (5–10 min bursts).
- Fallback behavior: if Private cluster under pressure, they want automated fallback to Redwood Hosted model with redaction and anonymization; must ensure no raw payload leaves their VPC unless explicitly approved.
- Audit/compliance: full request/response logs (redacted) + model versioning audit trail. Retention policy 90 days.
- Authentication: mutual TLS + client cert rotation policy; support for OIDC for user access.

Technical notes / gotchas mentioned by Meridian:
- They use tokenization: transaction payloads include token IDs that map in their internal vault. Need mapping orchestration so Redwood components do not retain mapping keys. Clarify whether we can provide a lightweight sidecar to perform de-tokenization inside their VPC.
- KV cache behavior: their fraud model benefit from long-lived KV cache per customer to reduce recomputation. Need clear memory/eviction metrics and how that maps to cost.
- Model quantization concerns: Meridian worried about quality regressions when using int8 quantized variants. They ask for an eval harness to run on their in-house test set before rollout.
- Networking: VPC peering vs Private Service Connect — Sara prefers PSC for simpler firewall rules, Tom prefers peering for throughput. Need to outline pros/cons and expected ports.

Action items / next steps:
- Alex: prepare SOW-style checklist for Private deployment (KMS/HSM integration steps, network options, minimum infra footprint, canary rollout plan, SLAs) — due 2026-04-05.
- Priya: draft eval harness template + instructions for running synthetic load and quality tests against quantized model variants; include perf regression thresholds — due 2026-04-07.
- Luis: capture expected resource sizing for 100 QPS baseline and 500 QPS burst (GPU count, memory, node sizing) and provide cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Private — due 2026-04-06.
- Meridian (Tom/Sara): provide sample (sanitized) transaction set and short list of critical failure cases for the evaluation; confirm KMS provider + HSM type — requested by 2026-04-08.
- Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive (network + KMS) with Meridian infra team: suggest Wed 2026-04-07 10:00 ET.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Can Redwood support sidecar de-tokenizer pattern in customer VPC? (impact: reduces exposure, complexity for us).
- Fallback policy: what constitutes "under pressure" for automated Hosted fallback? Need threshold (cpu/gpu util, queue latency) and an opt-in config.
- Audit trail retention: Meridian wants 90 days, but we need to confirm storage cost and retention export options.
- Model variant compatibility: which quantized variants are acceptable for their fraud thresholds? Need to run their eval.

Links + references mentioned on call:
- Confluence integration page: https://confluence.redwood/integrations/MB-123
- Internal jira: JIRA-4521 (Meridian private deploy pre-checklist)
- Example sidecar pattern doc: https://confluence.redwood/architecture/sidecar-de-tokenization

Meeting notes shorthand / personal TODOs:
- Prep a one-pager for Tom that maps network options (PSC vs peering) and call out firewall ports and egress behavior. Keep it 1 page.
- Add sample mTLS cert rotation cadence and exemplar terraform snippet to SOW checklist.
- Confirm that Hosted fallback can be configured with "no-raw-payload" mode where we only send redacted payloads; if not, flag as blocker.

Risks:
- If quantization introduces measurable lift in false positives → time-to-market delay. Mitigation: make quantization optional, include A/B canary.
- KMS/HSM integration complexity may push timeline if customer's HSM is uncommon. Build fallback guidance (bring-your-own-key vs proxy key store).

Status: draft. Will convert parts to shareable SOW and send to Meridian legal/infosec once internal review complete.

Contact notes: Tom best contact via email tom.ellis@meridianbank.com; Sara prefers Slack (workspace meridian-infra) for async questions.

File attachments to request from Meridian: sanitized transaction sample (CSV), HSM model/version, security questionnaire (completed).

End of notes.
